Executive Summary for the RMP

Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policy:
3V Sigma USA, Inc. is dedicated to providing every employee with a safe work environment free from conditions that could cause injuries, illnesses, or releases of hazardous materials. We will maintain a safety and health program that aligns with the best practices of similar organizations. The goal of our safety and health program is to exceed the best experiences of comparable operations. We aim for every employee to adopt the "zero-injury" philosophy: believing that every injury or illness is preventable and that no accidents are acceptable.  

Our preventative measures begin before any new chemical is introduced into the facility. Changes are reviewed at multiple levels, including safety and environmental impacts. Emphasis is placed on characterizing all incoming materials to determine the necessary protective measures for safe storage and handling. No chemical substance enters or leaves our facility without documented information detailing its hazardous properties and safe handling precautions. Our storage and processing equipment is designed to contain and manage the materials used safely. Design data and process evaluations are reviewed at several stages to ensure their completeness. Our ongoing programs to inspect, maintain, and improve our processes demonstrate 3V's commitment to keeping our employees, the surrounding community, and the environment safe.

Facility and Regulated Substances Handled:
The 3V Sigma USA, Inc. facility is located adjacent to the Sampit River, approximately 4.0 miles west of Highway 17 South on Woodstock Road in Georgetown County, South Carolina. The core business is dedicated to the batch production of organic specialty chemicals.  Customers range from the cosmetics industry to paper and pulp manufacturers. 

Our manufacturing process is quite similar across all products. Measured amounts of raw materials are pumped from storage tanks to a r

eaction vessel through a closed piping system. Sometimes, various additives and solid materials are loaded into the reactors via portals or dump chutes. The mixture is then reacted by adjusting the temperature and pressure within the reaction vessel. The resulting mixture is transferred to downstream equipment, where mechanical processes such as filtering, drying, and packaging take place. Any unreacted material is recovered for reuse or treated and removed. Generally, the storage, transfer, and reaction steps are the most critical for safety. Most of our final products are non-hazardous. 

3V stores two raw materials classified as covered chemicals under the RMP program. These materials include acetaldehyde and vinyl acetate. All substances are stored and processed in closed systems equipped with protective alarms and features. 

Worst Case Toxic Release Scenario For Process 1: [Vinyl acetate]
The worst-case release scenario for the toxic chemical, vinyl acetate monomer (VAM), was postulated to be a release from the largest VAM above ground storage tank, TK-104. The tank is 18,267 gallons and is administratively controlled to 90% capacity, or 16,440 gallons. The density of VAM used was 7.5 pounds/gallon therefore the quantity released was estimated to be 123,300 pounds. RMP*Comp Version 1.07 was used to estimate the endpoint distance of 0.3 miles. The supporting data can be found in the 3V Sigma USA PSM/RMP Compliance CSS 9056 Section 17 Table A-1.

Alternative Toxic Release Scenario For Process 1: [Vinyl acetate]
The alternative-case release scenario for VAM was postulated to be a hose break/disconnect during bottom unloading from a tank wagon to the storage tank outside the tank dike (truck side). The tank wagon holds 44,000 lbs. and takes 45 minutes to unload therefore the estimated release rate from the unloading hose is 900 lb./min.  RMP*Comp Version 1.07 was used to estimate the endpoint distance of 0.1 miles. 

Worst Case Flammable Release Scenario For Proce

ss 1: [Acetaldehyde]
The worst-case release scenario for the flammable substance onsite, acetaldehyde, was postulated to be a release from the acetaldehyde above ground storage tank, TK-507. The tank is 11,250 gallons and is administratively controlled to 90% capacity or 10,125 gallons. TK-507 is chilled and under pressure (up to 45 PSI). The density of acetaldehyde used was 6.6 pounds/gallon therefore the quantity released was estimated to be 66,825 pounds.  RMP*Comp Version 1.07 was used to estimate the endpoint distance of 0.3 miles. The supporting data can be found in the 3V Sigma USA PSM/RMP Compliance CSS 9056 Section 17 Table A-1.

Alternative Case Flammable Release Scenario For Process 1: [Acetaldehyde]
The alternative-case releases scenario for acetaldehyde was postulated to be a release from a hose break/disconnect during unloading from a tank wagon to the storage tank outside the tank dike (truck side). The tank wagon holds 28,000 lbs. and takes 60 minutes to unload therefore the estimated release rate from the unloading hose is 500 lb./min. RMP*Comp Version 1.07 was used to estimate the endpoint distance of <0.1 miles.

Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical-specific Prevention Steps:
All waste management, raw materials, and finished products operations are carried out with the necessary precautions to prevent accidental ignition or reaction of flammable or reactive materials. Smoking is prohibited throughout the facility. Hot work must be performed only with a permit and must not be performed near combustible materials. Process equipment and storage tanks containing flammable liquids are grounded, bonded, and inerted with nitrogen. Equipment is fitted with flame arrestors. Oxidizers and organic peroxides are kept separate from combustible and flammable liquids. Signs are posted at the facility entrance banning smoking, matches, or open flames. Facility personnel routinely inspect process vessels, pumps, and piping systems for leaks. Temperat

ures, pressures, and levels are monitored at appropriate intervals on tanks and process equipment. Containment structures surround tanks and process units containing hazardous materials to contain spills if they occur. These structures are inspected regularly, and any deficiencies are addressed as they are found. Storage tanks containing flammable or toxic liquids are equipped with nitrogen blankets to remove oxygen, vent controls to prevent over- or under-pressurization, and safety devices to prevent tank failure. The structural integrity of vessels, piping systems, and tanks is checked through visual inspections each shift for leaks and through scheduled non-destructive thickness testing at recommended intervals.

The acetaldehyde and vinyl acetate systems, along with all related manufacturing processes, are regulated under the OSHA Process Safety Management rule. As "covered" chemicals, they are assessed for safety from loading and storage through final processing. Hazard evaluations have been conducted for all equipment, procedures, and monitoring systems used to handle these chemicals. 3V's Process Safety Management program is fully implemented to prevent releases of these substances by incorporating the following features: 1) hazard identification, 2) protective measures, 3) procedures written to instruct employees on proper handling and operation, 4) control systems, 5) periodic equipment inspections and maintenance, and 6) training for all personnel involved in hazardous processes.  

The storage systems for acetaldehyde and vinyl acetate comply with NFPA standards for flammable liquids. These guidelines ensure that the tanks will not over-pressurize during emergencies. Some specific methods we use to prevent accidents include the following:

* Inerting - nitrogen is used to purge oxygen from tanks, pipes, and process equipment to eliminate the risk of a flammable atmosphere. Under inert conditions, flammable vapors cannot ignite.
* Grounding and Bonding - s

torage and process systems are grounded, bonded, and tested to prevent static discharges, which can be a potential ignition source.
* Venting - storage tanks and process vessels are equipped with emergency venting systems to prevent vessel ruptures, explosions, and structural damage in over-pressure situations.
* Alarms - storage tanks and process vessels are equipped with various alarms to alert personnel when an operating parameter (such as level, temperature, or pressure) falls outside its safe range. 
* Temperature Control - Acetaldehyde is stored at lower temperatures to decrease its vapor pressure, which helps prevent significant vapor release from the storage and transfer systems.

The Five-Year Accident History:
In the past five years, we have had no reportable accidents related to our regulated chemicals or their processes. This demonstrates our ability to safely manage these materials without endangering off-site populations.

The Emergency Response Program:
3V Sigma USA Inc. (3V) has a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan (Plan). The purpose of the Plan is to reduce hazards to human health or the environment from fires, explosions, or any unplanned release of hazardous materials into the air, soil, or surface water. 3V's Emergency Response Plan is provided to and reviewed with local emergency response agencies and is included in the Georgetown County Emergency Response Plan. Additionally, 3V has provided the LEPC and the local fire department with information about the facility's hazardous chemical inventory. On July 9th, 2025, SC DES reviewed the RMP rule for Process 1. No findings were issued.

All employees are trained to recognize the general facility evacuation alarm tones and to understand evacuation procedures and emergency response procedures specific to their work area. Additionally, employees who may be involved in a hazardous materials release are trained to identify dangerous materials and unsafe situations and to take defensive actions, such

as activating alarms, implementing containment, control, and evacuation procedures.  
Drill exercises are planned and scheduled to keep emergency response personnel current in their training and proficient in procedures and equipment use. 

Georgetown County participates in an independent local community alert network, with 3V Sigma USA, Inc. involved in that effort. In the unlikely event of a hazardous material release, potentially affected residents would be notified by telephone from a centralized service and given instructions on how to protect themselves.
